security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline SDK method names, and placeholder Azure endpoint examples. The value-printing examples are confirmed risks because copied code could expose configuration values in logs or terminal output. No prompt injection, malicious exfiltration intent, or hidden control instructions were found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace value-printing examples with redacted output or print only keys, labels, and content metadata.

remediation.issue: Connection string example includes a Secret placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note to prefer Entra ID in production and never paste real connection strings into prompts, logs, or source files.

remediation.issue: Operational examples omit logging safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short warning that App Configuration values may be sensitive and should be redacted in diagnostics.

content.user_title: Manage Azure App Configuration in Python
content.value_statement: Python teams need reliable examples for centralized settings and feature flags. This skill provides focused Azure App Configuration SDK patterns for common application workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the azure-appconfiguration Python package.
Explains connection string and Entra ID authentication patterns.
Provides examples for reading, writing, listing, and deleting configuration settings.
Covers labels, key filters, feature flags, read-only settings, and snapshots.
Includes async client setup and cleanup examples for Python applications.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not connect to Azure by itself.
Examples omit production error handling, retry policy, and observability details.
It does not replace Azure identity, RBAC, or Key Vault security guidance.
It does not include runnable tests or a complete sample application.

use_cases.title: Add Centralized Settings
use_cases.description: Use the SDK examples to move Python application settings into Azure App Configuration.

use_cases.title: Manage Release Flags
use_cases.description: Create and read feature flags for staged releases and environment-specific behavior.

use_cases.title: Prepare Deployment Snapshots
use_cases.description: Use labels and snapshots to capture production configuration before a deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure App Configuration client in Python using Entra ID.

prompt_templates.title: Read Labeled Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Python example that reads settings with a production label and groups them by key prefix.

prompt_templates.title: Add Feature Flags
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a feature flag workflow with safe defaults and clear rollout naming.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure App Configuration Python design for authentication, labels, snapshots, and logging risks.

output_examples.input: Request: Explain how to authenticate a Python service with Azure App Configuration.
output_examples.output: A concise recommendation to use Entra ID with DefaultAzureCredential, plus when a connection string may be acceptable.

output_examples.input: Request: Plan feature flag keys for a beta rollout.
output: Suggested key naming for beta features.
Recommended labels for development, staging, and production.
A note to avoid logging setting values during rollout checks.

output_examples.input: Request: Prepare a deployment rollback process.
output_examples.output: A workflow that uses labels, read-only production settings, and snapshots before deployment changes.

best_practices: Use Entra ID and least-privilege access for production services.
Separate environments with labels and clear key prefixes.
Redact configuration values in logs, examples, and support output.
anti_patterns: Do not store real secrets directly in App Configuration values.
Do not print all configuration values in production logs.
Do not use one label or key namespace for every environment.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides SDK usage guidance and examples for code that you run separately.

faq.question: Which Python package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the azure-appconfiguration package and related Azure identity client patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with feature flags?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for creating, reading, and listing Azure App Configuration feature flags.

faq.question: Does it handle authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows connection string and Entra ID patterns, with Entra ID preferred for production.

faq.question: Is this a complete production template?
faq.answer: No. You still need error handling, retries, monitoring, access controls, and secret management.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
